# CANDIDATE: VIX_INTRADAY_MEANREVERT_TO_VWAP
**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis
Intraday spikes in VIX often precede short-lived price deviations from VWAP that revert as volatility mean-reverts. The edge exists because VIX spikes reflect temporary imbalance in options demand, which can cause short-term price dislocations from fair value (VWAP) that correct as volatility mean-reverts and liquidity providers step in.

## Mechanism
Calculate the 5-minute VIX average; when the current VIX exceeds its 5-minute average by > 0.8 VIX points and the absolute deviation of price from the 1-minute VWAP is > 0.3% of price, enter a mean-reversion trade: go long if price is below VWAP, short if above, on the close of the bar where both conditions hold simultaneously. Exit shape: Stop set at 0.5% beyond the entry price opposite the trade direction; target 1 at 1× risk (aim to revert to VWAP); if price reaches VWAP, exit half and let the remainder trail with a 10-bar chandelier stop. Regime hint: Effective when overall VIX level is < 25 (to avoid regime-wide volatility shocks) and during mid-morning (10:00-11:30 ET) when liquidity is steady; avoid the first 15 min and the last 30 min of the session.
